concerns.text: The primary Tobit regression is described as fitting only the noise level (σ_noise) on the full dataset. It omits key covariates such as window size (T) and system dimension (N), which are known to influence Δλ. This omission creates a risk of omitted‑variable bias, undermining the ability to isolate the effect of noise.

The power analysis assumes 30 independent trials per cell and treats each FTLE observation as independent. However, the data are hierarchical (multiple sliding‑window FTLEs per trajectory) and autocorrelated, which reduces the effective sample size. The claim of ≥ 80 % power for a small‑to‑medium effect (f²≈0.02) is therefore likely overstated.

concerns.location: plan.md:Phase 6 – Tobit censored regression on full dataset
concerns.text: Censoring arises from the ‘unphysical’ flag (‖x‖ > 20.0), which is itself a function of the noise level. Tobit models assume censoring at a known, exogenous threshold; here the censoring mechanism is endogenous to σ_noise, potentially biasing the estimated noise coefficient.

concerns.location: plan.md:Phase 3 & Phase 4 – Baseline and FTLE computation
concerns.text: Δλ is defined as the difference between noisy FTLE and the clean‑system baseline. The baseline is computed on noise‑free trajectories only; any systematic shift in dynamics caused by noise (e.g., altered attractor geometry) is not captured, so Δλ conflates pure noise bias with baseline mismatch, threatening construct validity.
